title: Content-assert the references pinned only by filename, and restore the assertion spliced into a comment (#216 + #230 + #210)
objective: Close one defect at three addresses: a reference or an assertion pinned by a PROXY rather than by its property. #216 -- four badf-engineering-verification references (acceptance, integration-test-contract, non-coverage, verification-matrix) pinned by filename only. #230 -- six of badf-build's fourteen (acceptance, evidence-packaging, handoff-to-g08, preflight, retry-and-budget, stop-conditions) carrying no content assertion. #210 -- self.assertEqual([], entry['allowed_tools']) spliced into a trailing comment by a semicolon edit, so allowed_tools appeared exactly once in its module, inside a comment, and the guard ran for nobody. Being listed in a REFS set is a proxy for being content-asserted; the proxy was satisfied while nothing checked the text, so each file could be emptied to zero bytes and stay green.
business_value: A guard that cannot fail is not a guard. These are the enforcement surfaces that would catch a governance document being gutted or a registry entry silently acquiring tools -- exactly the drift the contract tests exist to refuse. Until this lands, eighteen references across two families and one allowed_tools guard are decorative. Closing the class at three addresses in one pass also avoids three PRs that would conflict with each other by construction on badf/lockfile.json.

note: Cluster of #216 + #230 + #210 as ONE WP: one defect class at three addresses. Deviation from one-issue-one-task is deliberate, follows BADF-QA's batching rule, and was endorsed by SARCHI as coordinator before work began -- three PRs would each re-sign badf/lockfile.json and conflict by construction. Ownership recorded for author!=reviewer: #216 is mine (fix existed unpushed since before this session; I flagged it twice then silently deprioritised it -- disclosed, not quietly cleared); #230 is BADF-QA's finding, ceded explicitly so they can review; #210 unclaimed, with BARCHI-2's courtesy yes on touching badf-build. The six were measured TWO independent ways -- empirical gutting and static read()-call analysis -- agreeing exactly, which carries information only because the instruments differ. test_obligations are declared at CONTRACT level, not unit: these assert frozen document content, so the accurate level is contract and BLD-I07/I08 C4's unit red-phase rule does not apply. Field names read from schemas/work-package.schema.json rather than copied from a sibling, after BARCHI-2 lost two composed-tree runs to invented test_obligations keys. Probes restore in a finally (BADF-QA), after an earlier killed probe left a reference gutted and contaminated its own baseline; that run was discarded and re-measured on a tree verified clean.
